title: Point-in-Time Certification for Alternative Data Vendors
one_liner: A vendor-paid, buyer-trusted forensic test that a dataset's history is genuinely point-in-time, extended to certify that an LLM-driven signal isn't leaking hindsight, plus a cheap timestamp 'witness' service.
customer: Mid-sized alt-data vendors and AI-signal startups ($2M to $50M ARR) selling to funds, at $15K to $40K per certification, about $8K per year to recertify, and $500 per month for the witness service. Fund data-sourcing teams use the reports free, which is what makes the badge valuable.
problem: Quants ask every vendor one question: 'when did you start collecting live?' The honest answer is usually that the history was reconstructed, with today's entity maps and taxonomies, overwritten revisions, and publication timestamps standing in for availability timestamps. Funds burn three to six months of trials before discovering this. Vendors lose deals, and every fund duplicates the same diligence. LLM signals add parametric hindsight, where the model's weights already know the outcomes of the backtest period.
solution: A standardized battery run on vendor samples under NDA. It tests for discontinuities at the claimed live date (coverage, missingness, revision rates, distribution shifts, entity-map consistency, timestamp-lag distribution) and for survivorship and delisting gaps. For LLM signals it runs black-box hindsight probes and entity-masked or post-cutoff re-runs. The output is a PIT Grade, a one-page badge and a machine-readable report. The witness service takes a daily cryptographic hash or snapshot of the vendor's feed, so in a year the vendor has third-party-provable live history.
why_now: Thousands of data vendors now sell into funds, banks and AI-agent builders who lack quant-grade diligence. 2025 to 2026 research (Look-Ahead-Bench, HindsightBench, detecting lookahead in LLM forecasts) has made LLM look-ahead bias a mainstream worry. Regulators are scrutinizing hypothetical and backtested performance claims.
revenue_model: Issuer-pays certification fees, annual recertification, a per-month witness subscription, and a premium hindsight audit for AI-signal vendors and allocators diligencing AI-driven funds.
non_obvious_insight: The only real proof of point-in-time history is a third party's timestamps, because vendor engineers routinely overwrite and backfill. Each buyer rediscovers this privately, so the cost is duplicated across hundreds of funds. Shifting the cost to the vendor, who wants the shorter sales cycle, is the arbitrage. Credibility requires published methodology and public aggregate fail rates, or it becomes a pay-for-grade scheme like pre-2008 ratings.
first_30_days: Open-source the PIT test suite on GitHub and publish teardowns of three public datasets. Get two or three fund data-sourcing heads to say they would use the reports. Sell five vendors a $7.5K 'pre-audit' in exchange for being named references, and launch the witness hash service to any vendor who asks.

title: Paid Caregiver Demonstration-Data Cooperative
one_liner: Home-care aides and family caregivers wear head cameras during non-intimate care tasks and earn revenue share from licensing that data to robot-foundation-model companies.
customer: Robotics labs and humanoid makers buying home-task demonstration data (Figure, 1X, Skild, Physical Intelligence, Generalist-class buyers), at $60-150 per usable hour. Home-care agencies are the distribution partner.
problem: Humanoid progress is bottlenecked on physical-world data. Data vendors already pay people to film themselves making coffee (XDOF about $50M annualized, Mecka projecting $100M ARR). Nobody has data on the hardest, highest-value home tasks: walker and transfer assistance, modified-diet meal prep, laundry and tidying around frail people. Meanwhile aides earn under $35k and agencies see 77-80% turnover.
solution: Give each aide a $150 camera kit and an on-device consent and blurring pipeline. Capture only task categories that avoid intimate care, with care-recipient or proxy consent per home. Pay a per-hour data premium on top of wages, which agencies use as a retention bonus, and sell curated, labeled datasets.
why_now: Robot data-as-a-service went from nothing to unicorn valuations in months (Sep 2026). Immigration crackdowns are draining the care workforce, so agencies are desperate for retention tools that do not raise Medicaid-capped rates.
revenue_model: License datasets at $60-150 per hour. Pay workers 30-40%, agency 10% and keep the remainder. Add curation and labeling fees.
non_obvious_insight: Robots cannot yet enter the homes that hold the training data they most need, but the lowest-paid workforce in America is already inside them. Data pay solves agencies' turnover problem at no cost to a squeezed Medicaid budget.
first_30_days: Sign one home-care agency and 20 aides for a pilot. Write a consent and privacy protocol with an elder-law attorney. Pre-sell a 500-hour dataset to one robotics lab using a sample of kitchen and laundry tasks.

title: Amnesty Desk: Legalizing Unpermitted Backyard Units
one_liner: Fixed-fee 'legalize your existing unit' service that is paid at closing, turning unpermitted ADUs and garage conversions into appraisable, financeable, insurable square footage.
customer: Homeowners (and heirs) with unpermitted ADUs, basement apartments or garage conversions built before the amnesty cutoff, plus listing agents who need the unit legal before it sells.
problem: Huge numbers of homes contain units built without permits. They can't be appraised as living area, financed, insured properly, or sold without discounts and buyer fear. Owners assume legalization means demolition or a full code retrofit, and city permit counters are unfamiliar with the new amnesty rules.
solution: Productized legalization. A paid feasibility scan (measured as-built drawing, life-safety checklist), then a fixed-price package covering plans, permit filing under the amnesty rules, inspection coordination and any minimal safety fixes. Offer a contingent, paid-at-escrow version for listing agents, and an appraiser-ready package that unlocks HELOCs or refinancing once legal.
why_now: California's AB 2533 took effect January 1, 2025. Cities generally must accept applications for eligible pre-2020 unpermitted ADUs and JADUs without retroactive penalties or full code upgrades, unless the unit is unsafe. Regional guidance was still being issued in March 2026. Some estimates say tens of thousands of additional units are now eligible. Local planning staff are still learning the process. More states are loosening ADU rules.
revenue_model: $1,500-2,500 feasibility and as-built fee, then an $8-15K legalization package. Alternatively a contingent fee of roughly 1% of the sale price paid at close for agent-referred listings. Referral fees from lenders and insurers once units are legal.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is city-by-city procedural knowledge, not architecture: how each of the roughly 500 California jurisdictions actually processes amnesty applications. The buyer of the outcome is often the next buyer, lender or insurer, so price and pitch it as a sale-price unlock ('an extra $80-150K of appraised value') rather than a permit fee. A database of how each city behaves is the compounding moat.
first_30_days: Pick 3 adjacent cities in one region (for example Bay Area or LA basin). Partner with a licensed architect or expediter and a measurement scanner. Build a one-page eligibility checker. Reach out to listing agents and to homeowners who have advertised unpermitted units on rental sites. Close the first 5 feasibility scans at $2,000 each and offer the first 2 legalizations at a discount for case studies.

title: Verified-Real Dating Portraits Shot by Wedding Photographers
one_liner: A consumer brand that rents wedding photographers' dead winter months to shoot candid-directed dating and profile portraits, delivered with a signed 'real photo' certificate.
customer: Single adults aged 25-45 in the top 20 US metros paying $179-299 per session. Secondary channel: matchmakers and dating coaches buying sessions for their clients.
problem: Wedding photographers earn most of their income in a compressed May-October window and sit mostly idle from November to March, with skills and gear already paid for. Meanwhile dating profiles are flooded with AI-generated and heavily retouched photos, so users and matches increasingly distrust every photo. Existing options are cheap AI headshot apps (the very thing everyone distrusts), generic corporate headshot studios that make stiff LinkedIn photos, and a few dating-photo studios with model-y aesthetics. Nobody is selling authenticity as a verifiable, human-shot product.
solution: A productized 60-minute walk-and-talk shoot across three locations using wedding-style directing prompts ('walk toward me and tell me the worst first date you've had') that get natural laughter from stiff people in about 90 seconds. Delivery is 15 edited photos in 48 hours following a dating shot list (full-body, hobby, social proof, pet, non-selfie smile). Each set ships with a 'Real Photo Certificate': Content Credentials (C2PA) from supported cameras, a no-generative-AI editing policy, and a public verification page users can link in their bio. Supply comes from wedding photographers trained in a 90-minute module. The platform handles booking, payment, brand, marketing and QC and keeps 30-35%.
why_now: AI-generated profile photos are now common enough that dating apps have leaned on photo and face verification. Several major camera makers now ship Content Credentials support in newer bodies or firmware, so provenance is technically feasible for small studios. Wedding photographers are also under margin pressure as couples trim coverage hours and guest counts, so winter income is increasingly attractive. 2026 is the first year 'proof a human made this' has real consumer value.
revenue_model: $199-299 per session with a 30-35% platform take. Upsells include a $39 'profile audit' and a re-shoot at 6 months. B2B2C packages for matchmakers and dating coaches at $150 per client.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce skill isn't lighting, it's getting a stiff stranger to laugh convincingly on cue, which wedding photographers do 40 times a summer. The photographer's marginal cost in January is close to zero, so supply arrives almost free while every competitor pays full-time studio rents.
first_30_days: Pick one metro and recruit 6 wedding photographers who complain publicly about winter. Run 20 pilot shoots at a $99 launch price, sourced from local Instagram/Reddit dating communities, run clubs and singles events, and from 5 matchmakers and dating coaches. Ask each client for before/after match counts (self-reported) and permission to publish testimonials. Register a public verification page for each set. Charge full price from shoot 21 onward.

title: Decoy Employees: Canary Tokens for People
one_liner: AI-run fake accounts-payable and help-desk staffers listed where attackers scrape, with voice agents that answer, harvest attacker infrastructure and alert the real team the moment anyone probes.
customer: Security teams at mid-market and enterprise companies in finance, healthcare and professional services, MSPs, and cyber insurers.
problem: Social-engineering crews research org charts and websites to find AP staff and help-desk numbers. Voice-deepfake defenses react only after the call, and defenders get no early warning that they are being targeted. Reports of successful voice-deepfake attacks are rising fast.
solution: Create decoy personas (an AP specialist, a help-desk line) that appear in the company's staff page, vendor portals and public contact lists, never on fake LinkedIn accounts. Each has a mailbox and a monitored voice agent that engages callers safely with no connection to real systems. Every contact triggers an alert with caller number, script, requested bank changes and voice samples, feeds the SIEM, and builds a weekly attack-tempo report for insurers.
why_now: Voice cloning and real-time voice agents make plausible fake clerks cheap. Vishing has surged and attackers automate reconnaissance, so deception is one of the few defenses that scales with attacker automation.
revenue_model: $1.5-3K per month per decoy set, MSP resale, and insurer partnerships.
non_obvious_insight: Canary tokens for files and credentials are standard, but canary employees are not. Decoys turn the attacker's reconnaissance into your telemetry, so the more the attacker automates, the more signal you get.
first_30_days: Build one persona pack with a voice agent and alerting. Deploy at 5 friendly companies with legal and HR sign-off, collect 30 days of hits as proof, and price a $1K per month pilot.

title: Tele-Operated Night Aides for Small Care Homes
one_liner: Metered remote-aide hours operating an off-the-shelf mobile manipulator robot in 6-16 bed residential care homes, so labor crosses borders when workers cannot.
customer: Owners of small residential care homes and assisted living homes (adult family homes, RCFEs) that run one awake overnight staffer, paying about $2,500-4,000 a month per home.
problem: Staffing is collapsing, with a 75-country visa pause, Haitian TPS loss and Wisconsin homes closing wings. One Wisconsin operator spent $100k+ on housing for overseas workers and then lost visa access. Small homes cannot buy robots or hire tech staff, and much aide time is walking, fetching and watching.
solution: Lease a wheeled mobile-manipulator (for example a Hello Robot Stretch-class unit) and pair it with remote aides, offshore or US-based. The remote aide handles night rounds, door and light tasks, supply fetching and two-way calming talk with dementia residents. The aide escalates to the on-site caregiver through a shared protocol. Do not touch medication or personal care.
why_now: Teleoperated home robots (1X NEO, Waymo-style remote centers) proved the model in 2025-26. Workers can no longer be moved, but work can. Occupancy is at a 19-year high with no new supply before 2030.
revenue_model: Monthly subscription per home covering robot lease plus a pool of remote hours. Overage billed per hour. Target unit margin of about 40% after remote-labor cost.
non_obvious_insight: Staffing rules count bodies on site, but most overnight risk is watching and fetching, which a remote human plus a modest robot can cover. The visa crackdown turns labor arbitrage into a physical-presence product.
first_30_days: Sign three care homes in one state that allow tech-augmented overnight staffing. Buy one robot and hire two remote aides. Run supervised night shifts and log fall and wandering response times as proof for the next 20 sales.

title: Verifier-Ready Emissions Data Rooms for CBAM Exporters
one_liner: A metering-to-evidence pipeline that gives small non-EU steel, aluminum and fertilizer producers a clean, pre-audited data room for accredited verifiers, so their EU and UK buyers stop defaulting to punitive default values.
customer: Producers and processors with 50-500 employees in Turkey, India, Egypt, Vietnam, Ukraine and South Africa (steel re-rollers, extruders, wire and fastener makers, fertilizer blenders). Paid by the producer or subsidized by the EU/UK importer buying from them.
problem: CBAM entered its definitive phase in 2026 and UK CBAM starts 1 Jan 2027 across 8 sectors. Importers lacking actual emissions data fall back on default values, which carry a mark-up (background, verify). Accredited verifiers are scarce, and small producers keep energy invoices in spreadsheets with no monitoring plan, so verification is slow and expensive and importers cannot get usable data.
solution: A two-week onboarding: connect electricity and gas meters or invoices, production logs and precursor traceability, then generate the monitoring methodology plan, the emissions report in CBAM format and an evidence index. Internal pre-verification, hand-off to partner verifiers, quarterly refresh, and sharing of the verified data with each importer through an API.
why_now: The definitive period began in 2026, verification of 2026 imports lands in 2027, and UK CBAM begins in three months. Default-value cost pressure now exceeds the price of proper data collection.
revenue_model: EUR 6-25k/year per plant (producer-paid or importer-sponsored supplier program) plus a coordination fee per verification.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone sells CBAM to the EU importer's finance team. The bottleneck is evidence-poor factories and verifier capacity upstream. Importers will fund supplier readiness because default values cost more than the tool, and verified plant data is reusable across every EU and UK customer of that plant.
first_30_days: Find three EU or UK importers of steel wire or fasteners with Turkish or Indian suppliers (trade fairs, LinkedIn) and offer a supplier-readiness pilot for five plants at EUR 3k each. Deliver with templates and spreadsheets and partner with one or two verifiers.

title: Hype-Item Triage for Thrift and Charity Shops
one_liner: A 10-second back-room scan station that tells thrift and charity staff which donated sneakers and collectibles are worth $150 instead of $12, then lists them online for a revenue share.
customer: Independent Goodwill regionals, church and charity thrift shops, Plato's Closet-style franchisees, consignment shops and estate-sale companies. They pay a rev share on the uplift, or $199 per month per store.
problem: Thrift pricers are paid to move volume and price shoes at a flat $8 to $25 by category. Meanwhile teen and adult resellers ('pickers') walk the racks right after restock and buy the $12 pairs worth $200 and up. Donations are the shop's raw material, and the shop is giving the profit to the pickers. Charities lose real money, and staff cannot read a style code or tell a real pair from a fake, so they either underprice or avoid the risk.
solution: A tablet at the sorting table. Staff photograph the tongue tag or box label. OCR pulls the style code and size, then the app returns resale value, days-to-sell, condition-adjusted price and known fake tells for that model. Anything over $60 goes into an 'online' bin. Our remote team of college and teen resellers lists, ships and remits the shop's share, so the shop needs no e-commerce staff. Later categories: trading cards, LEGO, vintage tees, Stanley cups, Pokemon sealed product, watches.
why_now: Thrift has boomed with Gen Z while tariffs push shoppers to secondhand, which also means more pickers hitting the same racks. Multimodal models now read tag photos accurately and cheaply. Donations arrive in volume, but shop margins are squeezed by picker competition and labor costs. Charities have never had a hype-specific tool.
revenue_model: 20% to 30% of net sale price on items routed to online, or a SaaS fee per store. Charities are motivated because it is found money for their programs.
non_obvious_insight: The biggest sneaker sourcing channel for resellers is a flat-price system that cannot see value. The knowledge needed is tiny: style code, size, box, one authenticity tell. That is why resellers win, and it can be sold to the seller side. Being reseller-native gives me trust with staff and the sourcing instincts to know which categories are next.
first_30_days: Offer three local charity thrift shops a free two-week pilot. I sort through their back room on a Saturday, list the top 30 items, and split proceeds with the charity (charity 70%, us 30%). Track the uplift versus what those items would have sold for on the floor. Turn the numbers into a one-page case study and pitch 20 more independent thrift operators.

title: Waiver-Funded Home Modification Back Office and Factoring
one_liner: Handle the prior-authorization paperwork and advance payment for small contractors who do ramps and bathroom retrofits funded by Medicaid waivers and VA grants.
customer: Small accessibility and remodeling contractors (3-15 employees) in states with waiver home-modification benefits, plus case managers and AAAs who can't find bidders.
problem: Senior housing supply is stuck through 2030, so aging in place is structurally favored and home mods are the cheapest fix. But waiver and VA HISA funding needs OT assessments, multiple bids, packets, inspections and 60-120 day payment, so good contractors avoid it. Approved seniors can't find anyone to do the work.
solution: A back office that prepares the packet (OT evaluation scheduling, standard scope, photos, bids, permits), tracks approval, submits invoices, and advances 85-90% of payment within five days against the approved authorization. A network directory shows case managers which contractors are ready to bid.
why_now: 41 states have HCBS waitlists over 600k, so states favor cheap home-based solutions over $115k-a-year nursing home stays. Medicaid cuts and 15-month waits add pressure, while 80+ growth means demand for mods is up.
revenue_model: 3-5% packet fee, a 1.5-3% factoring spread, and a platform fee from states or MCOs for a ready-to-bid contractor pool.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck for funded home modifications is contractor cash flow and paperwork, not consumer demand or budget. Fixing the contractor's experience creates supply where the money already exists.
first_30_days: In one state, recruit five contractors and process 10 packets. Secure a small credit line from a CDFI or SBA lender to fund advances, then approach the state's HCBS case management office.

title: At-Home Feline Urine Lab via Smartphone
one_liner: A non-absorbent litter collection kit and phone-camera strip reader that flags early urinary, diabetic and kidney-related changes in cats and routes trends to the clinic.
customer: Owners of senior cats, male cats with prior urinary blockage and diabetic cats, sold through clinics; clinics running senior and chronic-care programs.
problem: Cats hide illness. There are 53M US cat households (39%), multi-cat homes are growing fast, and only about 2% of cats are insured. Urinary obstruction and kidney disease produce costly emergencies. Urinalysis needs a clinic visit and a clinic-collected sample, so it is skipped.
solution: Starter kit with collection litter, a tray, dipsticks and a calibration card. The app reads strip colors on-device, tracks trends per cat, sends clinic-set alerts (blood, protein, glucose, pH shifts) and offers one-tap booking. Later: a phone-readable specific-gravity attachment and multi-cat pairing with existing smart litter boxes.
why_now: On-device colorimetric ML has matured, and smartphone-read at-home urine tests already exist for humans. Vets have become comfortable with home-generated data through CGMs, and cat households are the fastest-growing pet segment, while clinics need reasons to see patients earlier.
revenue_model: $29-49 starter kit plus about $12 per month refills sold through clinics with a 30% clinic margin. Diet-company sponsorship and insurer wellness programs later.
non_obvious_insight: The industry keeps building smart litter boxes to infer health from motion and weight. Chemistry is a cheaper and more informative signal, and cats produce the sample daily; the barrier was collection and interpretation, not sensing.
first_30_days: Validate dipstick plus phone reading against clinic urinalyses on about 100 cats in 2 clinics. Build a minimal app with the calibration card. Sell 200 kits through 5 clinics and measure adherence and alerts that led to visits.

title: Actual-Play Sessions Turned Into Animated Episodes
one_liner: A pipeline that turns a tabletop RPG stream's audio and character art into a condensed animated episode using the cast's own voices, with human review.
customer: Actual-play shows and TTRPG creators with 3k-50k Patreon patrons, and TTRPG publishers wanting marketing series.
problem: Fans want animated adaptations, but animation costs millions. Creators have hundreds of hours of audio and no way to give patrons a visual product.
solution: Ingest the session audio and each creator's character art bible. An LLM editor condenses a 4-hour session into a 12-20 minute script. Video generation uses per-character references trained only on the creator's own art, with consenting voices and lip-sync, and a producer reviews each cut. Output includes premium-tier episodes and short clips for growth.
why_now: Video models now generate consistent characters with synced audio, and creators can use their own art and voices with disclosure, which sidesteps most of the AI-slop backlash.
revenue_model: $1.5-5k per episode or 20-30% of new patron revenue for 12 months, plus a licensing fee for publishers.
non_obvious_insight: The output is not cinema but the recap format, the 'previously on' fans share, and the same pipeline produces shorts that grow the channel. Consent and disclosure are the differentiators.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 mid-size actual-play creators. Produce one 90-second pilot for each from public sessions, and refine. Sell 3 paid episodes at $1.5k.

title: 1098-VLI Reporting for Small Auto Lenders
one_liner: Turn a loan tape into IRS-ready Form 1098-VLI statements, with VIN validation and U.S.-final-assembly flags, for credit unions, community banks and buy-here-pay-here dealers that cannot wait for their core vendor.
customer: Credit unions, community banks, CDFIs, independent auto finance companies, buy-here-pay-here dealers and their loan servicers. Any trade or business receiving $600 or more in interest on a qualifying vehicle loan must report, and the statute has no small-lender exemption. The lender pays per form and per VIN cleanse.
problem: Treasury's final regulations under IRC 6050AA (published Sept 8, 2026; effective Nov 9, 2026) require Form 1098-VLI showing borrower TIN, interest received, opening principal, origination date and the vehicle's year, make, model and VIN. Statements are due to borrowers by Jan 31 and to the IRS by Feb 28 (Mar 31 if e-filed), with penalties under 6721 and 6722. Transition relief covered 2025, so the 2026 tax year is the first full-form season. The preamble concedes lenders 'may need to collect additional information' and 'may experience difficulties accurately reporting the VIN'. Treasury declined to make lenders verify U.S. assembly, allowing reliance on the VIN plant code or the manufacturer's final-assembly label.
solution: The lender uploads a CSV from its core or loan origination system. The service validates VIN check digits, decodes them through NHTSA's free decoder, and maps plant-of-manufacture codes through a curated plant-to-final-assembly table it maintains. It screens for new versus used, personal use and origination date, and checks TIN completeness. It produces an exception queue (missing or wrong VINs) with borrower outreach templates. It then generates and delivers the 1098-VLI statements and e-files with the IRS. A white-label web widget for lender sites answers 'is my loan deduction-eligible?'
why_now: The regs were finalized Sept 8, 2026 and take effect Nov 9. Statements are due Jan 31, 2027, giving four months. Big core processors will serve their largest clients first, and 2026 is the first year without a simple summary-statement safe harbor. The consumer deduction (up to $10,000 of interest on new, U.S.-assembled vehicles under the 2025 tax law) means borrowers will call their lenders asking whether their car qualifies.
revenue_model: $2-4 per form with a $1,500 annual minimum. $0.25 per loan for VIN cleansing and exception handling. Enterprise license for servicers and core-vendor partners. Consumer eligibility widget with lead-gen to tax preparers or refinance offers.
non_obvious_insight: Treasury turned a bright-line rule into a data-quality problem and pushed the risk to the lender. Whether a car is American-assembled is answered by plant-code tables and labels, not by anything in a lender's servicing system, and the preamble openly warns of VIN reporting difficulties. The moat is a curated plant-to-final-assembly table plus an exceptions workflow, which the big vendors will treat as an edge case for small clients. Source: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/09/08/2026-18219/car-loan-interest-deduction (final regs on 6050AA reporting, Form 1098-VLI, the $600 threshold, no small-lender exemption, and the VIN and plant-of-manufacture provisions).
first_30_days: Build the VIN pipeline on NHTSA's free decoder and validate it on 1,000 real VINs. Offer 30 credit unions a free VIN readiness audit on a 500-loan sample tape and show them their error rate. Publish a plant-code explainer for CU and community bank newsletters. Sign three design partners through state credit union leagues and CUSOs, with a goal of $10k in prepaid annual minimums by December.

title: Defense Magnet and Tungsten Provenance Dossiers
one_liner: A shared investigator that produces audit-ready provenance files on magnets and tungsten parts for the sub-tier suppliers who cannot get answers from their distributors.
customer: Small and mid-size defense sub-tier suppliers (motors, actuators, sensors, drones, speakers) that buy NdFeB, SmCo magnets or tungsten parts through distributors.
problem: DFARS magnet and tungsten sourcing restrictions extend to upstream mining and refining stages from January 2027. Small suppliers cannot compel Chinese-linked distributors or sinterers to disclose provenance, and primes will demand attestations.
solution: A dossier per part family: supplier questionnaires, document and mill-cert review, distributor-to-sinterer trace-back, and optional lab fingerprinting (trace-element and isotopic) via partner labs. It includes an attestation vault ready for prime audits and an approved-source list of non-covered and recycled suppliers.
why_now: The January 2027 DFARS deadline is about three months away as of late September 2026. Government equity deals (MP, Lithium Americas) and the BIS scrap rule show that provenance is now a national-security control.
revenue_model: $4-15K per part family, $1-3K monthly subscription for upkeep and alerts, and lab-test pass-through with margin.
non_obvious_insight: This is a paperwork problem too small for any customer to solve alone. A shared investigator with a growing fingerprint library amortizes the cost across dozens of clients and gets cheaper as it scales.
first_30_days: Build a free 'does this part need proof?' checker. Pull sub-tier contractors from public procurement records and reach out to 100 firms with the January deadline. Line up a partner lab for fingerprinting. Close 5 paid dossiers.

title: The Master's Letter Apprenticeships
one_liner: Six-week, premium apprenticeships with master craftspeople that give teens the one credential AI cannot counterfeit: a named human's signed, callable letter about what they actually did.
customer: Affluent parents of 15-18 year olds (private-school and college-admissions-anxious) paying $6-12k per placement. Masters (luthiers, boat-builders, stone masons, pastry chefs, bookbinders, restoration carpenters, farriers) get 60% of tuition.
problem: Application essays are AI-contaminated, and admissions offices are shifting to in-person writing, short answers, and interviews because they can't trust take-home work. Wealthy families are hunting for hard-to-fake, embodied, verifiable experiences. Meanwhile master craftspeople in aging trades lack apprentices and income to take them on.
solution: A curated roster of about 40 masters per metro. Structured 6-week apprenticeships on real work, not shadowing. Each ends in a finished object with the maker's mark and a Master's Letter written to a rubric, backed by a recorded interview and a verification page colleges can call. An alumni network and independent counselors' referral fees drive supply of students.
why_now: Admissions officers openly discount take-home writing and are moving to formats that are harder to fake. Entry-level white-collar hiring is shrinking (Stanford payroll data show early-career workers in AI-exposed jobs losing ground), which raises the prestige and perceived safety of craft. Aging masters have shops and no successors.
revenue_model: 25-40% platform fee on $6-12k tuition. Corporate- or foundation-sponsored scholarship seats. $900 'Family Master Day' add-ons.
non_obvious_insight: The product isn't the skill. It is a third-party attested effort signed by a reputationally exposed human. A letter from a master who stakes their name is the analog of the old handwritten recommendation, now scarce. The supply side is an underused asset: elderly masters with empty workbenches.
first_30_days: Recruit 8 masters in one city through trade guilds. Publish a landing page. Recruit 5-10 independent college counselors as referral partners at 10%. Sell 12 slots for summer 2027 starting in the winter admissions-anxiety season. Get background checks and liability insurance in place.

title: Menu Trial Lab: Restaurants as Food-Brand Test Sites
one_liner: A network of two-to-five-unit restaurants that run randomized menu experiments for food brands and commodity boards, and get paid for it.
customer: Emerging food and beverage brands (sauces, blended or alternative proteins, beverages), commodity checkoff boards (beef, pork, dairy, potato, avocado and similar), and distributor private-label teams pay $10-25k per trial. Independent operators are paid a fee and free product and get menu-engineering results back.
problem: Foodservice launches fail because the operator's ROI is unproven, not because guests dislike the item. Line speed, storage, training, plate cost and cannibalization decide whether an item survives. Brands pay for sales reps, menu-placement deals and consumer surveys, but survey data measures stated preference. The item then sits in my walk-in. Reps tell operators 'it sells' with no data to prove it.
solution: Recruit a network of 2-5-unit independents who connect Toast, Square or Clover. Each trial is a randomized matched-pair test: the item is on the menu at one location and not at its twin, then swapped, and we run a difference-in-differences on attach rate, check average, cannibalization, plate cost and contribution margin per cover. The deliverable is a 'Menu Adoption Scorecard' plus an operator-facing ROI one-pager the brand's reps and distributors can use to close accounts. Automated matched-pair design and automated POS reading keep unit costs low.
why_now: Beef, coffee, cocoa and dairy cost pressure has kept operators reformulating (blends, substitutions) since 2025, and brands need proof under tighter budgets. POS platform APIs and partner ecosystems now make continuous read access practical at scale. AI makes experiment design and reporting cheap. Commodity boards and distributors are under pressure to show operator-level ROI. I could not verify whether an existing network already sells this, so check Datassential, Technomic and distributor pilot programs first.
revenue_model: Fee per trial ($10-25k) paid by the brand or board, with a portion (say $500-2,000) paid to each participating operator. Later, annual data subscriptions for brand teams and 'scorecard' licensing to distributors.
non_obvious_insight: A two-location owner is a natural experimenter, since it is the only cheap way to run a true A/B with identical kitchens, menus and staff. Nobody in food innovation uses that. The buyer's real question is 'will an operator make money and keep it on the menu', which no consumer panel answers. The moat is the operator network and their POS data, not the analytics.
first_30_days: Post in owner Facebook groups and a regional restaurant association to recruit 10 two-to-five-unit operators, including my own two locations as pilot sites. Approach 5 emerging brands at a regional foodservice show with a $5-8k, four-week matched-pair trial. Run my first trial in my own two restaurants and turn the results into a 3-page scorecard to use as the sales collateral for the next brand.

title: Predict Walk-In Cooler Failures Via Refrigeration Techs
one_liner: White-label predictive monitoring that local commercial-refrigeration companies sell as a maintenance plan, so a failing compressor becomes a Tuesday service visit rather than a Saturday-night emergency.
customer: Independent commercial refrigeration and HVAC-R service companies with 5-50 techs, who pay roughly $8-12 per monitored compressor per month and resell at $25-40 inside a maintenance plan. The restaurant is the end payer. A later add-on is a spoilage-insurer premium discount.
problem: A walk-in dies on Saturday at 9pm. That means an emergency call at 2-3x the rate and $8-15k of protein and dairy in the dumpster, sometimes a closed kitchen. Temperature-probe alerts only fire after the box is already warm, so they are too late. The real early signals are in the power draw: rising duty cycle from dirty condenser coils, failing fan motors and capacitors, low charge, short-cycling, and defrost heater faults. Techs spend their weekends on emergencies and have almost no recurring revenue.
solution: Clip-on current-sensing hardware (roughly $25-40 bill of materials) with a cellular or Wi-Fi gateway on each compressor and condenser fan. A model compares duty cycle and amp draw against ambient kitchen temperature and defrost cycles to flag drift weeks before the box warms. It creates a scheduled work order in the contractor's dispatch system (for example ServiceTitan) with the likely fault and parts to bring. The contractor sells it as a 'Sunday-proof plan' and gets the white-label dashboard and monthly reports.
why_now: Cellular IoT and current sensors are very cheap. Field-service software has spread through small trades, so integrations are possible. Skilled refrigeration techs are scarce and contractors need each tech to cover more boxes. The HFC phasedown (AIM Act) is changing refrigerants and service complexity, pushing repair-versus-replace decisions. Power prices are climbing, so efficiency drift now costs owners visibly.
revenue_model: Recurring B2B2B: $8-12 per monitored compressor per month to the contractor, plus hardware at cost and a per-contractor platform fee. Later, add insurer partnerships that pay for verified spoilage-loss reductions.
non_obvious_insight: The real distribution channel for restaurant equipment tech is not SaaS marketing to owners. It is 'my guy': the one refrigeration tech who answers his phone. Owners trust him, he holds the keys and the relationship, and he hates 2am calls and lacks recurring revenue. Sell to Mike, not to me. The signal is also cheaper than probes: amp draw predicts failures that temperature only reveals when it is too late.
first_30_days: Instrument 10-15 compressors and condenser fans across my two locations and five friends' restaurants with off-the-shelf clamp sensors. Log data and record every failure. Sign 2-3 local refrigeration companies as design partners with a free 60-day pilot of 50 sensors. Use the first 'caught it before Saturday' event as the case study, then sell the plan to that contractor's other accounts.

title: Jobsite Translator That Teaches the Trade
one_liner: Live English-Spanish translation for construction crews that also logs each worker's vocabulary and safety instructions, turning toolbox talks into comprehension-verified training and a path to licensure.
customer: Mid-size specialty contractors (electrical, drywall, framing, roofing, concrete) with mixed-language crews, their safety directors, and union or association training funds.
problem: OSHA expects training delivered in a language and vocabulary workers understand. Language gaps cause incidents and keep capable helpers from advancing to licensed journeyman. Supervisors cannot verify comprehension, and ESL classes do not teach jobsite vocabulary.
solution: A phone and earbud app: real-time two-way translation with trade-specific glossaries, personalized micro-lessons built from each worker's actual jobsite phrases, comprehension checks after toolbox talks with signed training records, and an upskilling track toward licensing-exam vocabulary.
why_now: Consumer earbuds with live translation shipped in late 2025 and LLM translation now handles jargon with supplied glossaries. Labor shortages make retaining and upskilling existing crews more valuable.
revenue_model: $15-25 per worker per month paid by contractors, training-fund reimbursement, and a safety-compliance bundle.
non_obvious_insight: Translation removes the barrier in the moment, but the durable value is converting translated moments into a personalized curriculum and compliance record. The trade workforce is a captive, unserved learning audience, and safety compliance is an existing budget line.
first_30_days: Pilot with 2 contractors that have largely Spanish-speaking crews. Use the app in the weekly toolbox talk, then hand the safety director a comprehension-verification report. Charge $20 per worker and test on noisy sites early.

title: Youth-Slang Drift API for Safety Teams
one_liner: A continuously updated, human-verified lexicon and drift detector for Gen Alpha and teen slang, coded risk terms and grooming language, sold as an API to moderation and school-safety teams.
customer: Trust-and-safety teams at game and social platforms, K-12 student-monitoring vendors, school-safety directors, and moderation stacks inside AI toys and companions.
problem: Youth language shifts every few months. Classifiers trained on last year's data misread banter and miss coded terms for sextortion, self-harm and grooming. School monitors bury counselors in false alerts. As bans push kids into private chats and games, moderation teams are older and further from the language.
solution: A lexicon with context tags (benign, hazard, coded-risk; severity; platform of origin; age range), plus alerts when a term's usage or meaning shifts, delivered via API and a weekly briefing. It is built with a paid panel of consented 16-19-year-old language scouts (parental consent where needed) and linguists.
why_now: Age-gated platform tiers, bans and duty-of-care laws raise the cost of missed threats. Moderation is now LLM-based and needs fresh context that models lack. Volume and speed of Gen Alpha slang keep growing.
revenue_model: $2-15k a month per platform or vendor for API and briefings, plus custom lexicon builds.
non_obvious_insight: LLMs know last year's slang, so freshness is a data-supply problem. The moat is the paid youth panel and labeling process, not the model.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 teens (with parental consent) and 3 linguists. Publish a free monthly 'Gen Alpha threat lexicon' for trust-and-safety newsletters. Land 2 design partners, one school-monitoring vendor and one kids' game, at $1k a month each.

title: Contrast Capture: Recovering Iodine From Post-Scan Urine
one_liner: Capture iodinated and gadolinium contrast agents from patients' urine at CT and MRI centers, funded by the drug makers who now owe EU wastewater EPR fees, and recover the iodine and gadolinium.
customer: Contrast-media producers and their EPR schemes (the payer), imaging centers and hospital radiology departments (the host), and water utilities. Start in the Netherlands, Germany, the Nordics and Switzerland.
problem: Contrast agents are excreted almost entirely unchanged within about a day, pass through conventional wastewater treatment, and show up in rivers and drinking water (anthropogenic gadolinium anomalies are documented near large cities). The recast EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive now requires pharma and cosmetics producers to fund at least 80% of quaternary treatment costs. Treating a whole city's effluent for one class of molecule is expensive and contrast agents are very persistent. Meanwhile iodine (tens of grams per contrast CT) and the rare earth gadolinium are supply-concentrated materials being flushed away.
solution: At-source capture in radiology: single-use polymer-lined urine bags or urine-diverting toilets in the imaging suite, handed out at check-out with a prepaid courier or bin for the first voids. A central facility recovers iodine and gadolinium by ion exchange and crystallization and returns them to producers as recycled input. The product sold to producers is 'verified kilograms of contrast removed from the water cycle', a metric their EPR schemes can count against fees. Hospitals get a 'green radiology' certification.
why_now: The recast UWWTD (Directive 2024/3019) is in force and producers are beginning to work out how to meet the 80% cost share, so source-control measures are being sought now. Rare-earth and critical-materials recovery is politically fashionable, giving hospitals and funders a second reason to say yes.
revenue_model: Per-patient capture fee paid by producers or their EPR fund (a few euros per scan), plus sale of recovered iodine and gadolinium (worth roughly $1-3 of iodine per contrast CT, so it supplements rather than carries the business), plus utility co-funding contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The materials are worth pennies to a few dollars per patient; the real revenue is the avoided cost of tertiary and quaternary treatment plants, and the party who owes it is not the hospital but the drug companies. A waste business with a pharma-industry payer.
first_30_days: Sign letters of intent with two imaging centers and one water utility in the Netherlands or Germany. Run a 200-patient pilot with off-the-shelf urine bags and a university lab to measure capture rates and patient compliance. Present the data to the producers' trade body and to the EPR scheme designers as a candidate 'innovative measure' needing pilot funding.

title: Credit Union Tokenized Deposit Network
one_liner: Give thousands of small credit unions a shared 24/7 tokenized-deposit settlement network so they can answer the 'war for deposits' together instead of losing it one by one.
customer: Credit unions ($500M-$10B assets), state leagues and CUSOs, and later their members and local merchants.
problem: Banks describe the stablecoin fight as a '$6 trillion war for deposits' (CoinDesk, 2026-09-14). No single credit union has the scale to run its own token or build 24/7 settlement, and Zelle-style networks are controlled by big banks. Members get weekday-hours payments between institutions.
solution: A CUSO-owned network of tokenized member deposits (not a stablecoin at first), starting with 24/7 credit-union-to-credit-union settlement for shared branching and member P2P, then bill pay and merchant acceptance. A licensed trust-bank or custody partner handles the token layer and reserves.
why_now: The OCC charter wave (Circle 2026-07-10, Coinbase April, Bridge and Crypto.com conditional) has made compliant token infrastructure available to partner with. Citi and Coinbase launched corporate stablecoin acceptance on 2026-09-28, and the GENIUS Act takes effect around Jan 2027 (verify).
revenue_model: Network transaction fees, SaaS to member credit unions, and a share of reserve income on the settlement layer.
non_obvious_insight: The cooperative structure is the unfair advantage. Credit unions already share ATMs, branching and core processing through CUSOs, so a shared money layer is a natural extension that gives 4,500 small institutions scale none could build alone.
first_30_days: Get LOIs from five credit unions through one state league. Run a paper pilot for inter-credit-union treasury settlement with a partner trust bank, and charge pilot fees for design work and integration.

title: Rare Blood Group Assay Foundry
one_liner: Turn each newly recognized blood-group gene into research-use genotyping controls and panels for reference labs, starting with the MAL deletions that define AnWj-negative blood.
customer: Immunohematology reference labs, rare-donor programs and blood centers. Blood-group genotyping platform vendors that want to add content are a second buyer.
problem: AnWj-negative patients, over 99.9% of people are AnWj-positive, can form antibodies against AnWj and risk serious transfusion reactions from ordinary units, and compatible donors are 'extraordinarily difficult' to find. Antibody testing finds the patients but cannot identify rare genetic carriers or donors. Volumes are too small for large diagnostics companies to prioritize.
solution: A small molecular-biology team designs, validates and sells RUO kits: synthetic positive-control DNA for the published MAL deletions, primer and probe sets, and a small validation panel. It then repeats the process for each new ISBT system or rare antigen as the genes are published. It also licenses content to genotyping platform vendors and offers a sample-testing service for rare-donor registries.
why_now: MAL was formally recognized as ISBT blood group system 047 in 2026, and the authors say genotyping tests 'can potentially be incorporated into existing blood group genotyping systems.' Nobody has yet turned the finding into a commercial assay. Cheap gene synthesis and long-read or targeted sequencing make a low-volume, high-value control kit practical for a small team.
revenue_model: RUO control and primer kits at roughly $500-2,000 each, per-sample testing fees for registries, and content-licensing or royalty deals with platform vendors. Later, a CLIA or LDT lab service.
non_obvious_insight: Every new blood-group gene discovery creates a diagnostic gap that big vendors ignore because volume is tiny, and the 47th ISBT system was only just recognized. The NHS Blood and Transplant discovery took nearly 20 years and states that serological testing 'cannot identify rare genetic cases without genetic sequencing' (https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/09/260918024828.htm; Blood 2024, DOI 10.1182/blood.2024025099). A repeatable foundry that converts each new ISBT gene into a control kit captures a stream of these gaps. Rare-donor matching is a high-willingness-to-pay niche because a single unmatched patient can cost a hospital far more than a kit.
first_30_days: Design gBlock-style synthetic controls for the MAL deletion alleles reported in the Blood paper and validate them on public or donated DNA. Contact the NHS Blood and Transplant IBGRL, the American Rare Donor Program and 5-10 US and EU reference labs to trial the RUO kit. Line up a second gene from the recent ISBT additions. Pitch two platform vendors on a content deal.

title: Exit Ramps for Dying AI Platforms
one_liner: A converter plus fixed-price migration service that turns Flowise flows, OpenAI Agent Builder graphs and Assistants API integrations into portable, regression-tested code.
customer: AI automation agencies that have 5-50 client agents built on Flowise, Agent Builder or the Assistants API, and in-house AI teams at SMEs that have no engineer to spare. They pay per migrated agent.
problem: Three AI platforms are being killed within about 90 days. The Assistants API shut down on 26 Aug 2026. Agent Builder shuts down on 30 Nov 2026. Flowise was archived in mid-Aug 2026 and its core team leaves on 31 Aug. Non-technical teams built visual flows they cannot maintain as raw code. A Flowise insider says forkers 'own dependency updates, security patches, and model API churn indefinitely, and the contributor community that used to absorb that work is dispersing.' A commenter says telling non-engineers to maintain a TypeScript codebase 'is not a real answer.'
solution: Build importers for Flowise chatflow JSON, Agent Builder workflow exports and Assistants objects (assistants, threads, vector stores, files). They feed a neutral intermediate representation. Exporters then emit (a) Agents SDK / Responses API code, (b) n8n workflows, (c) Langflow. The differentiator is a parity proof. Historical conversation logs are replayed against old and new stacks, and the agency receives a behavioral-diff report it can send to its client. The output is plain, readable code that a coding agent such as Claude Code can maintain. Flowise itself says developers are moving to coding agents because 'rigid workflow low code approach quickly hits the limit.'
why_now: The Assistants API shutdown (26 Aug 2026), the Agent Builder deadline (30 Nov 2026) and the Flowise archive (Aug 2026) all land in one quarter, which forces spending on a real deadline. Coding agents now make code-first output maintainable by non-experts. Flowise has 55.5k stars and 25k forks, so the stranded installed base is large.
revenue_model: Fixed-price migration of $500-2,500 per agent. An agency plan of $199/mo keeps flows mirrored in the intermediate representation with a nightly 'can I still leave?' test. The free converter CLI is the lead magnet.
non_obvious_insight: The demand is a deadline plus a maintenance gap, not a tooling gap. Evidence: OpenAI's deprecations page gives the Agent Builder shutdown as 30 Nov 2026 and the Assistants API as 26 Aug 2026 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations). Flowise's sunset notice sets the code freeze, the archive and the end of core-team support (https://flowiseai.com/sunset). The GitHub repo shows 55.5k stars, 25k forks and 699 open issues (https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise). The HN thread quotes the 'not a real answer' complaint and notes that OpenAI's own Agent Builder is also going away (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49176920). Agencies that resell agents to clients are the buyers, and they carry portfolio risk that a single hobbyist does not. The parity report is what they sell on to their clients.
first_30_days: Week 1: mine the Flowise Discord, GitHub issues and r/n8n for stranded users. Ship a free 'flowise-to-n8n / Agents SDK' CLI that handles the 3 most common node types. Weeks 2-3: cold-DM 40 agencies and sell 5-10 pilot migrations at $750, prioritizing Agent Builder users before the 30 Nov deadline. Week 4: turn the manual steps in those migrations into automated exporters and publish before/after parity reports as case studies.

title: MCP Connectors for Emerging-Market Government Portals
one_liner: The maintained tool layer, with a human fallback network, that lets agents file taxes, e-invoices and registrations in Kenya, Nigeria, India, Mexico and Brazil.
customer: Bookkeeping and accounting SaaS, SME lenders, fintech onboarding teams and agent builders operating in Kenya, Nigeria, India, Mexico and Brazil.
problem: Agent tool ecosystems (MCP registries, Composio) index US SaaS APIs. In emerging markets the highest-value SME tasks, such as tax filing, e-invoicing, company registration and customs, live behind government portals with no API, monthly UI changes, captchas, OTPs and sometimes biometrics or paper stamps. Agent builders cannot reach 99% task completion, so agent products stall at the portal.
solution: Build and continuously test connectors (MCP servers) for Kenya's iTax and eTIMS, Nigeria's CAC and revenue-service portals, India's GST and MCA, Mexico's SAT/CFDI and Brazil's Receita and gov.br. Add a human fallback pool of cyber-cafe operators and licensed accountants who complete steps the agent cannot (consented OTP relay, captcha, in-person stamps). The buyer pays per successful filing, with a maintenance SLA.
why_now: The Ninth Circuit's 'the agent is the user' ruling and MCP's move to the Linux Foundation legitimize agents acting through user-authorized sessions. E-invoicing mandates (Kenya eTIMS, Brazil NF-e, Mexico CFDI, India GST) create recurring filing volume. Composio's $25M Series A shows the tool layer is fundable, and no one is building it for the Global South.
revenue_model: $0.50-3 per successful transaction, plus a monthly connector subscription per market ($200-1,000), plus a premium for the human-completion SLA.
non_obvious_insight: Connector maintenance is the moat because portals change monthly and nobody glamorous wants to own that. The human fallback converts 70% automation into 99% completion, which is exactly what fintech buyers pay for. The cyber-cafe operator, the old human middleman, becomes the agent's last-mile API.
first_30_days: Build Kenya iTax/eTIMS and Nigeria CAC connectors first. Sign three bookkeeping or SME-lending startups as design partners at a per-filing price. Staff the human fallback yourselves for the first 500 filings and log every failure type to prioritize automation.

title: Book-Not-Shop Roll-Up of Retiring Machine Shops
one_liner: Buy retiring shops' customer books, programs and drawings on earn-outs, then migrate the work to a partner network.
customer: Owners of 5-40 person machine shops aged 60+ who want a clean exit. The buyer's customers keep their supply.
problem: About 60% of US manufacturing firms have owners aged 55+, about 150k small and mid-size firms are near retirement, and customers often leave when the owner retires (per American Machinist and MMS). MMS admits no dataset exists. Existing buyers such as Compass Precision buy whole shops with real estate, iron and payroll, which is capital-heavy and risky.
solution: Buy only the customer relationships, drawings, programs, fixtures and quality records for about 1-1.5x annual gross profit, paid mostly as an earn-out on retained revenue over 24-36 months. The owner runs a transition site for 6-12 months. Work then moves to 3-5 partner shops that have spare capacity. Equipment is auctioned or leased. AI digitizes quote history and setup sheets.
why_now: The retirement wave is under way and PMI at 55.6 (highest since May 2022) keeps demand steady. PE roll-ups have proven that a market exists, and a capital-light structure fits smaller teams.
revenue_model: 15-25% gross margin on migrated work. Slotting fees from partner shops. Deal capital is $250-750k per deal, mostly as earn-out.
non_obvious_insight: The asset is customer trust and tacit programs, not buildings or machines. An earn-out tied to retained revenue makes both sides fight the main failure mode of roll-ups, which is customer attrition.
first_30_days: Build a list of 300 target shops from state registries, LinkedIn and outreach. Sign three LOIs on owner-friendly terms. Line up three partner shops with capacity. Raise a $1M search-fund-style pool or use SBA financing.

title: Mod-Approved Human Panels for Rare Audiences
one_liner: A research-recruitment service that turns Reddit's hardest-to-reach niche communities into bot-proof, mod-approved survey panels, with participants paid directly and the community getting the results back.
customer: UX and market research teams at health-tech, B2B SaaS and pharma patient-insights groups, boutique research agencies, and academic labs that need rare respondents (night-shift nurses, HVAC techs, POTS patients, first-time landlords, small-farm owners). Projects run $3k-$25k.
problem: Mainstream panels are being contaminated. A PNAS paper showed an autonomous AI survey respondent passing 99.8% of 6,000 standard attention checks. Rare-audience recruiting already costs $100-$300+ per complete and is slow. Researchers try recruiting in subreddits, but mods delete nearly every third-party survey post because of spam, data-harvesting fears, no ethics statement, no give-back, and no sample cap. Researchers get banned, and mod teams drown in survey modmail.
solution: A standardized 'research request kit': ethics and data-handling statement, incentive amount, sample cap, screener, and a commitment to post a plain-language results summary back to the community. Mods get a free Devvit intake queue with a checklist so approval takes about 60 seconds. Participants are paid directly (gift cards or PayPal), and nothing is paid to mods or communities, which respects Rule 5. Respondents can opt in to prove community tenure through user-consented OAuth (account age and history in that sub) plus a short liveness check and behavioral AI-agent detection. Buyers get a fraud-audit report with the data.
why_now: Agentic AI now beats standard survey quality checks (PNAS, late 2025), and research teams are actively looking for provably human samples. Reddit's five-community moderator cap, enforced from 31 March 2026, has thinned experienced mod teams, so requests that arrive pre-vetted and standardized are far more likely to be approved than cold modmail.
revenue_model: Per-complete pricing of $40-$150 (participant incentive $15-$60, gross margin roughly 35-45%), a $1.5k recruitment setup fee per project, annual retainers for repeat research teams, and a paid 'verified human' audit add-on.
non_obvious_insight: A mod team's approval plus demonstrable community tenure is a stronger anti-bot screen than any attention check, because aged, niche-active accounts are expensive to fake at scale and community norms punish liars. Mods say no for three fixable reasons (no results back, no data promises, no cap), so fixing those makes them say yes. The buyer's real pain isn't cost per complete but the fear that their data is silently synthetic.
first_30_days: Write the request kit and a one-page ethics template. Recruit 10 mid-size niche mod teams (10k-300k members) through mod Discords and existing goodwill, offering the intake queue free. Land 3 paid pilots from UX consultancies or academic labs at a 30% discount in exchange for case studies. Run three studies of about 100 completes each. Publish a side-by-side fraud audit against a conventional panel sample. Review Reddit's Data API commercial terms first, and keep responses collected off-platform.
